nodes.label: Business OS Seven-Check Activation Standard
nodes.rationale: All seven checks must pass before activation, and monitoring is deliberately manual in v1 with explicit automation triggers (25 active accounts, two early degradations in 90 days, or 8 operator hours/month). Any future automation must preserve HighLevel's separate authentication and must not mirror customer data into Syntholo.

nodes.label: Unaccredited PDF Certificates
nodes.rationale: Issuance is driven purely by lesson-completion state, independent of purchase tier or support window. No public verification lookup, certificate ID system, or accreditation claim exists in v1, which avoids implying credential authority the program does not have.

nodes.label: Commercial Offers, Refunds and Disputes
nodes.rationale: An unconditional seven-day refund releases seats and marks grants refunded without deleting the account, progress, certificates, or audit events. An open Stripe dispute creates an administrative hold that blocks new purchases and invitations while preserving learning access, so commercial state changes never destroy customer history.

nodes.label: V1 Exclusions
nodes.rationale: Automated AI coaching, native workflow builder, HighLevel SSO or mirrored data, mobile apps, gamification, and multilingual content are excluded so v1 delivers a human-supported implementation program instead of an automated platform.

nodes.label: No Public Certificate Verification Surface
nodes.rationale: Rejected as an explicit v1 non-goal: private authenticated member download plus audited staff-assisted redelivery satisfies delivery without creating certificate identifiers or a lookup surface. Account teammates cannot fetch one another's certificate.

nodes.label: Circle Community Isolation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Circle owns posts, comments, reactions, files, and moderation content; Syntholo exposes only a single handoff route with access-sync state. A Circle failure produces pending/failed sync and dead-letter work without blocking Academy or support.

nodes.label: Curriculum Readiness Gate
nodes.rationale: Payment creation stays blocked as CURRICULUM_GATE_BLOCKED unless the current production course has exactly 18 ready published lessons with an automated pass and a human approval bound to the same content hash. Any content change invalidates the approval by hash, and the public offer cache can never enable payment.

nodes.label: HighLevel Isolation Boundary
nodes.rationale: No API client, webhook, credential, SSO/session exchange, embedded surface, or customer-data mirror exists; the external URL is an environment-approved HTTPS origin plus opaque path carrying no Syntholo token or customer query data. Business OS state never creates, revokes, pauses, or checks Academy grants.

nodes.label: AI Operating System Academy
nodes.rationale: Positioned as a practical, human-supported implementation program (safe AI rules, three workflows, 90-day plan) rather than a passive video library, so the product surfaces emphasize visible human help over automation.

nodes.label: GNU Unifont 15.0.04 Certificate Fonts
nodes.rationale: Unifont is bundled unmodified and subset by the PDF renderer at generation time; the SIL OFL 1.1 branch of its dual license is chosen so the fonts can be embedded and redistributed with the product.

nodes.label: SIL Open Font License 1.1
nodes.rationale: Permits embedding, bundling, and redistribution of the font with software provided reserved names are not reused; the requirement to stay under this license does not extend to documents created with the font, which is why generated certificate PDFs are unencumbered.

nodes.label: ProductionMemberDashboard Client Component
nodes.rationale: The narrow "use client" root because @clerk/react exposes the bearer only in the browser and no approved server token bridge exists. getToken() is called immediately before each request and the bearer is never stored in state, context, storage, a URL, or a cookie; a second Next Route Handler BFF is rejected as another token-bearing hop.

nodes.label: Route-Module Ownership and Composition
nodes.rationale: Route adapters do only auth, validation, cache headers, and translation; schemas live in packages/contracts, transitions in packages/domain, persistence in scoped packages/database repositories, provider adapters in packages/integrations. No plugin is mounted under two identity verifiers, and worker/cron handlers are never exposed as HTTP routes.

nodes.label: Same-Origin /v1 Rewrite Facade
nodes.rationale: The browser calls relative /v1/** paths and Next.js applies a beforeFiles external rewrite to the separately deployed Fastify origin, preserving status, body, Location, Set-Cookie, Cookie, and Authorization without enabling credentialed CORS. Neither origin is inferred from forwarded request headers.

nodes.label: Clerk Member Authentication
nodes.rationale: Exactly one raw Authorization bearer is parsed; cookie-only, malformed, duplicate, staff-cookie, and mixed credentials are rejected. authenticateRequest is restricted to session_token, the configured audience, and an exact authorized party, and receives a cookie-free Request so no ambient cookie can authenticate a member.

nodes.label: Root CLAUDE.md AGENTS.md Import
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is a single `@AGENTS.md` include so that one agent-instruction source of truth serves both Claude Code and generic agent tooling.

nodes.label: Identity and Session Boundary
nodes.rationale: Consumer and workforce identity stay separate: neither issuer can cross the other API surface, and provider claims never become internal account, membership, or staff identifiers without an active PostgreSQL mapping.

nodes.label: Account-Scoped Member Dashboard Slice
nodes.rationale: Adds GET /v1/member/dashboard as a read-only composition over the existing Clerk actor, AccountRepository, and effective-access port. It returns only real foundation facts plus explicitly typed unavailable/empty downstream projections so the first production member home is honest rather than fixture-complete.

nodes.label: Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: The installed Next.js version has breaking changes versus model training data, so agents must read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ before writing code. The block is auto-regenerated by `next dev` via generate-agent-files.js, so committing it with the work keeps the tree clean rather than fighting a recurring uncommitted diff.

nodes.label: Web App Next.js Agent Rules Block
nodes.rationale: Duplicated inside apps/web because in a monorepo the `next` package may not resolve from the repo root; the guide path must resolve relative to this file's directory.
nodes.norm_label: web app next.js agent rules block

nodes.label: Collapsed 401 Identity Response
nodes.rationale: authenticateMember deliberately collapses an expired bearer and a valid Clerk identity with no PostgreSQL actor into one 401, so the UI must say it could not connect the sign-in to an active member account rather than asserting no account exists. Splitting provider auth from actor resolution belongs to the commerce claim contract.

nodes.label: createDatabase
nodes.rationale: Rejects connection URLs containing the PostgreSQL `options` key in any encoded, case-varied, or duplicate spelling, and sets object-level startup options forcing row_security=on with app.account_id empty. This overrides ambient PGOPTIONS so a host process cannot pre-seed an account ID or disable row security.

nodes.label: requireRecentAuth
nodes.rationale: Reads only a privately registered canonical millisecond scalar rather than the public authenticatedAt Date DTO, so Date.setTime on a structurally similar actor cannot upgrade authority. Unregistered or unavailable freshness fails closed.

nodes.label: useReverification Client Wrapper
nodes.rationale: The member fetcher acquires a bearer per invocation and translates only 403 RECENT_AUTH_REQUIRED into Clerk's documented reverification hint with level first_factor and afterMinutes 5. Clerk then reopens its UI and retries; cancellation remains a denial and no route pretends token renewal alone supplied reauthentication.

nodes.label: Pool Selection Boundary
nodes.rationale: The API verifies a token and resolves an internal actor before selecting a pool; pools are separate objects with separate URLs. Code must not authenticate with an owner URL and then use SET ROLE as pool selection, because that would make privilege depend on application code rather than the connection identity.

nodes.label: Anonymous Principal Cookie
nodes.rationale: A server-issued random 128-bit cookie carrying no user data is the stable retry/idempotency scope for anonymous writes. Raw IP is only a short-lived secondary abuse signal, never the sole principal, and no browser fingerprint or persisted raw IP is built.

nodes.label: Opaque Cursor Pagination
nodes.rationale: The cursor encodes the route's immutable filter set and stable sort tuple so a filter-mismatched cursor returns 400 INVALID_CURSOR rather than silently paging a different result set. Offset pagination is excluded from v1.

nodes.label: Idempotency-Key Contract
nodes.rationale: Scoped to (actor or anonymous principal, method, route template, key) with a canonical request hash, so a replay returns the original response without a second mutation, audit event, outbox event, notification, provider call, or capacity change. Webhooks instead key on (provider, providerEventId).

nodes.label: R5 Recent-Authentication Requirement
nodes.rationale: Trusted provider authentication time no more than 300 seconds old, mandatory for ownership transfer, seat replacement, Pilot decisions, publish/archive, refund approval, certificate redelivery, Business OS activation, and replay. A client-supplied timestamp never satisfies it.

nodes.label: Raw Webhook Signature Rules
nodes.rationale: Only the Stripe and Mux routes enable Fastify raw body; exact received bytes are verified before JSON parsing or domain dispatch, and the (provider, eventId) claim precedes mutation. Request logging and body capture are disabled so payloads and signature headers never reach logs, Sentry, or analytics.

nodes.label: Clerk factorVerificationAge Recent-Auth Derivation
nodes.rationale: Because fva is whole minutes, the API subtracts (fva[0]+1) minutes from token iat and compares that fixed instant with request time, so elapsed token age is included and a newly issued token does not reset factor age. Missing, malformed, fractional, or negative values fail closed.

nodes.label: ADR: Canonical v1 REST Route Contract
nodes.rationale: The focused plans fixed 15 paths but named the other command families without REST shapes, so client work, Zod contracts, authorization tests, and migrations would have started against locally invented paths. One v1 contract is fixed up front to prevent that divergence.
nodes.norm_label: adr: canonical v1 rest route contract

nodes.label: Rejected Generic /commands Endpoint
nodes.rationale: A single RPC-style endpoint would weaken route-level WorkOS permissions, raw-webhook isolation, rate limits, OpenAPI/Zod contracts, cache rules, and audit ownership. Verb paths like /approvePilot were also rejected because they expose implementation verbs and fragment list/history ownership; explicit plural subresources (decisions, publications, activations, replays) preserve command intent while keeping durable records addressable.

nodes.label: canonicalizeAccountName
nodes.rationale: NFC, trims only leading/trailing ASCII SPACE, preserves internal spaces, bounds 1-255 UTF-8 bytes, and rejects an explicit forbidden code-point set rather than silently trimming, so tab, NBSP, bidi/zero-width controls, surrogates, and noncharacters can never be stored.

nodes.label: isCanonicalAccountName
nodes.rationale: Used as a non-transforming response predicate so malformed stored data fails 500 rather than being silently repaired on read.

nodes.label: MemberDashboardResponse Contract
nodes.rationale: All Zod strict() objects with biconditional invariants tying experience.state to nextBestStep.kind, so neither producer nor consumer can drift. Membership role is deliberately absent because the pre-snapshot actor role can be stale across ownership transfer.

nodes.label: syntholo_account_name_is_canonical (SQL)
nodes.rationale: An immutable, strict, parallel-safe SQL function whose numeric code-point denylist is byte-for-byte reviewed against the TypeScript helper, deliberately avoiding locale-defined [:space:], \\s, or 'printable' regexes that would diverge between runtimes.

nodes.label: Migration 0008_account_name
nodes.rationale: Adds the immutable canonical-name predicate plus a write trigger that normalizes NFC and ASCII edge spaces before the check, preserving migration-first and rolled-back-API compatibility while new writers adopt the shared canonicalizer. Only member_api and migrator may execute the predicate.

nodes.label: Migration Renumbering Decision
nodes.rationale: Foundation migrations through 0007 are immutable and the dashboard slice claims 0008, so all focused-plan product migrations shift upward. No 0001-0007 file is renamed and no lower-numbered migration may be inserted after a higher number reached a shared environment; deployment order stays migration, API, worker, web.

nodes.label: Identity Production Launch Gates
nodes.rationale: Production is blocked until evidence records canonical host, WorkOS callback, embedded Clerk paths, provider instances/keys/audience, MFA and session policy, a staging token-schema capture that records no token material, key ownership/rotation operator, deployed /v1 proxy conformance, and PostgreSQL runtime-login topology attestation.

nodes.label: Demo Mode (Northstar Advisory Workspace)
nodes.rationale: Demo mode uses a deterministic fixture workspace and never contacts vendors, so local development and visual regression can run without provider credentials or side effects.

nodes.label: Demo DashboardView Separation
nodes.rationale: DashboardView embeds fixture-centric non-null assumptions (Maria, Northstar, a lesson, artifacts, a coach reply, a live session). Adapting production data into it would silently manufacture those records, so parallel production contracts and components are built and migrated card by card with no casts between the two types.

nodes.label: Production Launch Gate
nodes.rationale: `APP_MODE=production` is explicitly not a launch approval; a SHA-bound engineering gate plus independent migration/API/worker/cron processes, image and deployed-proxy evidence, provider settings, protected branch, and named operational owners are required so a config flag can never substitute for verified readiness.

nodes.label: acquireMemberReadClient
nodes.rationale: Because pg.Pool 8.23.0 exposes no public cancellation for a queued checkout, the wrapper keeps handlers on the original promise: a late-delivered client is immediately release(true)'d and a late rejection is consumed. connectionTimeoutMillis remains only a longer secondary guard whose untyped error is never translated.

nodes.label: MemberReadClientLease
nodes.rationale: Single-owner wrapper with idempotent release() and destroy() so repository finally blocks never double-release a raw client. It awaits the client `end` event plus settlement of the raw query within a 1,000 ms cleanup budget before the route may send its error.

nodes.label: runMemberReadQuery
nodes.rationale: Races the raw query against its own monotonic timer; on timeout it poisons the lease, calls the public typed PoolClient.release(true) which ends the client and destroys the socket, consumes the late rejection, and only then rejects with the sentinel. AbortSignal, Client.cancel, and query_timeout are explicitly not used as the cancellation mechanism or classifier.

nodes.label: translateMemberReadDependencyError
nodes.rationale: Exactly four instanceof allowlist entries (pool-acquire, query, parent, lock sentinels). Mapping every database exception to 503 would turn RLS regressions, malformed snapshots, and evaluator bugs into apparently routine outages, so raw SQLSTATEs, transport errors, and unknown exceptions stay 500. No code or message matching participates in classification.

nodes.label: Stable Error Envelope and Status Mapping
nodes.rationale: `details` is optional and allowlisted and must never carry provider payloads, tokens, stack traces, names, emails, transcripts, or artifact data. Cross-account or non-visible resources return 404 so no route reveals whether another account's ID exists.
nodes.norm_label: stable error envelope and status mapping

nodes.label: Two-Phase Encryption Key Rotation
nodes.rationale: Deploy the new active key while retaining every old decrypt key, let sessions re-encrypt or age out, verify no row references the old version, then remove it in a later deployment. Removing an in-use key is a fail-closed logout, not a recovery mechanism.

nodes.label: Staff PKCE Login Attempt Flow
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL stores only state/nonce hashes and an AES-GCM encrypted verifier with a five-minute one-use deadline and allowlisted relative return path. The callback consumes the attempt atomically and sign-out winning a race fences the callback, so a replayed or racing callback cannot resurrect a session.

nodes.label: Refresh Lease and Compare-and-Swap Rotation
nodes.rationale: Completion is accepted only for the current lease/version, before lease/session/new-token expiry, and while revoked_at is null. WorkOS invalid_grant is terminal and revokes locally, while network/timeout/408/429/5xx is transient and never authorizes an expired token.

nodes.label: WorkOS Staff Session and Cookie
nodes.rationale: Production staff authority is one host-only __Host-syntholo_staff_session cookie; the browser receives only a random 32-byte credential whose SHA-256 hash is the database lookup key. Tokens are stored as one AES-256-GCM bundle with AAD binding lookup hash, staff identity, and WorkOS session, so a stolen row cannot be replayed elsewhere.

nodes.label: Bounded Member-Read Deadlines
nodes.rationale: Pool 2s, query 5s, advisory lock 2s, whole dependency phase 8s, cleanup 1s, all enforced by repository-owned monotonic timers against an absolute performance.now() parent deadline rather than an AbortSignal, so no read waits indefinitely on Neon, the pool, or the entitlement lock.

nodes.label: attestSystemDatabase
nodes.rationale: Startup and command-time attestation of schemas, database CREATE/TEMP, object ownership, membership, table/column ACLs, and exact routine signatures, so a drifted system role fails closed rather than silently gaining authority.

nodes.label: Append-Only Audit Enforcement
nodes.rationale: Audit UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE are rejected by ENABLE ALWAYS triggers even for the table owner and migrator, and the ACLs omit those commands. Because a database owner could still drop the trigger with DDL, owner/DDL credentials are treated as a trusted operational boundary and never a runtime credential.

nodes.label: Five PostgreSQL Capability Roles
nodes.rationale: Group roles are NOLOGIN/NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS so a runtime login inherits exactly one capability and can never bypass RLS. Roles are created by SQL in a controlled admin session rather than the Neon Console/CLI/API, because Neon-provisioned roles inherit neon_superuser whose BYPASSRLS invalidates the whole boundary.

nodes.label: Migration 0004 Durable Jobs and Outbox
nodes.rationale: Leased SKIP LOCKED claims, per-attempt random fences, bounded retries/dead letters, atomic outbox-to-handler dispatch, and recoverable (handler_name,event_id) receipts. outbox_events.id is retained as a synchronized compatibility identity during rolling release while event_id becomes the primary domain identity.

nodes.label: syntholo_migrator Capability Role
nodes.rationale: A migrator admin policy exists because a non-bypass capability holding table grants would still be blocked by forced RLS. Migrations run only through a dedicated direct Neon owner/migration login, never a transaction-pooled URL.

nodes.label: syntholo_staff_api Capability Role
nodes.rationale: Staff policies on customer tables are read-only with cross-account SELECT; raw commerce and entitlement tables are not staff-readable, so admins with entitlements:manage must go through narrow list/claim/resolve functions and coaches see no provider, billing, token, or decision history.

nodes.label: syntholo_system_api Capability Role
nodes.rationale: Receives no DDL, ownership, alternate-schema, column, or non-allowlisted routine authority; a paid provider command runs only through createSystemUnitOfWork after attestSystemDatabase, and ordinary createUnitOfWork rejects a system actor.

nodes.label: syntholo_worker Capability Role
nodes.rationale: No account, member identity, membership, or staff identity access and cannot delete operational rows. Job/outbox access is only through fixed-search-path claim, lease-renewal, transition, dispatch, receipt, and fenced audit functions with no direct table grant.

nodes.label: Runtime Login Startup Attestation
nodes.rationale: Startup recursively attests current_user = session_user, exactly one expected NOLOGIN capability with INHERIT TRUE / SET FALSE / ADMIN FALSE, and no other reachable role, then independently resolves that capability OID/name and rejects LOGIN, privileged flags, role/database settings, and transitive outbound authority.

nodes.label: Accessibility and CSS-Only Motion Rules
nodes.rationale: All motion is CSS-only and globally disabled under prefers-reduced-motion; status and selection must stay understandable through visible text so no meaning is carried by animation alone. WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and 44px targets are hard floors, including for dense admin tables.

nodes.label: Four-Surface Experience Architecture
nodes.rationale: Public, Member, Coach, and Admin are separated as distinct surfaces so authorization, identity provider, and data exposure boundaries line up with product surface boundaries.

nodes.label: Guided Command Center
nodes.rationale: Member home gives exactly one action primary emphasis using a fixed precedence (access issue, coach reply, session within 48h, next lesson, incomplete artifact, feedback, then optional recommendation) so the member is never asked to choose among competing calls to action.

nodes.label: Human Support Model
nodes.rationale: Owner plus two teammates share one coach inbox with a two-business-day first substantive reply and one active artifact review per business, bounding coach load while keeping the promise of visible human help. There is deliberately no automated AI coach in v1.

nodes.label: Semantic Action Color Tokens
nodes.rationale: Teal means default primary action, coral means a human is involved, gold marks milestones, navy carries emphasis when teal is already active. Color is never the only signal so the meaning survives color-blindness and reduced-motion contexts.

nodes.label: Trusted Growth Visual System
nodes.rationale: Interprets Uxcel's learning-product hierarchy (quiet navigation, one dominant continuation task, small recommendation area, visible human help) without copying its branding, illustrations, text, or component geometry, keeping the identity premium/calm/human while avoiding sci-fi and corporate-gray cliches.

nodes.label: External Support-State Union
nodes.rationale: Root ruling: the external union is exactly new|assigned|waiting_on_coach|waiting_on_customer|resolved|closed. Storage may normalize an active thread to an internal `open` lifecycle, but `open` is an implementation detail and contract tests reject it at the response boundary.

nodes.label: Next-Best-Step Composer
nodes.rationale: Pure and server-owned, returning an action key rather than copy or a URL. Unavailable is a precedence barrier: treating it as empty could recommend a lesson or community action while an unanswered coach request or near-term session exists, so a sparser dashboard is accepted as the only sound result.

nodes.label: Unavailable-versus-Empty Projection States
nodes.rationale: `empty` may be emitted only after a successful authorized query proves absence; an adapter must never emit empty merely because its table, provider, or query is missing. The first deployed adapter always emits unavailable/module_not_implemented for all five projections.

nodes.label: AccountRepository.getById
nodes.rationale: The only exported customer read for accounts. It applies both the account scope and an explicit accounts.id predicate and returns null for a cross-account ID, revealing neither existence nor fields. There is deliberately no unscoped member-runtime account read or list method.

nodes.label: createUnitOfWork
nodes.rationale: The canonical member mutation boundary: validate the account UUID, begin on the member pool, set transaction-local app.account_id via parameterized set_config, expose only frozen transaction-bound repositories, then commit or roll back. RLS remains an independent second check so a scope bug alone cannot leak rows.

nodes.label: member_actor_for_clerk_user
nodes.rationale: A fixed-search-path security-definer function executable only by the member capability and migrator. It filters Clerk provider, active account, active membership, and exact provider user ID, returns at most one actor, cannot enumerate accounts, and does not weaken normal account RLS.

nodes.label: withAccountScope and DatabaseTransaction Internals
nodes.rationale: Kept package-internal and off the root exports so use-case callbacks cannot obtain raw Drizzle, builders, pool clients, or set_config and therefore cannot escape the account scope.

nodes.label: getMemberDashboard
nodes.rationale: Reads the informational account first and makes the advisory-lock-protected effective-access call the LAST database read, so a revocation or suspension committing in between fails the request. The reads must not run in parallel and generatedAt is captured only after final revalidation.

nodes.label: Member Effective-Access Reader Lock Protocol
nodes.rationale: Pins one connection, takes a session-level shared account advisory lock before BEGIN REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY, revalidates account and membership, then evaluates a frozen snapshot. Writers take the matching exclusive account-first lock so a response is wholly before or wholly after a writer, never a hybrid or post-commit stale snapshot.

nodes.label: syntholo_member_api Capability Role
nodes.rationale: Has no DELETE privilege or policy anywhere and no read access to audit, outbox, jobs, staff identity, or provider receipts. Any future member operation must add both a command-specific grant and a matching scoped policy in the same migration so an accidental grant alone cannot activate an existing FOR ALL policy.

nodes.label: expectedVersion Optimistic Concurrency
nodes.rationale: A typed expectedVersion field is used rather than If-Match so stale writes return 409 VERSION_CONFLICT with safe current-version metadata and never expose another member's private draft or body.

nodes.label: Syntholo-Dashboard-Version Negotiation
nodes.rationale: Body schemaVersion alone would break strict v1 clients when a v2 union appears, and silently mapping an available record to empty could select an unsafe lower-priority action. A header negotiates a frozen representation adapter with mandatory rollout order: dual-parser web, then v2 API, then the v2-requesting web switch.
